Choosing Among Contraceptive 
Methods- Key Counseling Questions
• How important is it to you to avoid pregnancy now?
• What contraceptive do you want to use?
• What methods have you used?
• Do you have any health issues?
• Do you want your use of contraception to be private?
• When (if ever) do you want to have a child?
• Does your partner want to have children in the future? When?
• Will your partner help you using condoms and/or paying for 
contraceptives?  Using abstinence when you don’t have another 
method?

Most Effective: Sterilization
Male- Vasectomy
 Erection/ejaculation 
unchanged
 Back-up method until sperm 
count negative
 Only 50% pregnancy rate 
with reversal
 Prostate Screening-detection 
bias
Female
 Tubal ligation-blockage or clipping 
of fallopian tubes
 Many MDs refuse if woman has 
not had child already
 30-70% risk of ectopic pregnancy 
with failure
 15% risk of hysterectomy later in 
life
 Decreased risk of ovarian CA
 $18000 to reverse- not covered by 
insurance
 72 hour wait post consent.

Intrauterine Device: IUD
 One of the highest patient 
satisfaction among methods
 Rapid return of fertility
 Safe
 Long-term protection
 Highly effective
 May be inserted after delivery 
or abortion
Extremely 
Effective

• Can be used:
 99% effective if placed within 5 days of intercourse
 Women with multiple partners
 Women with history of STDs or PID 
 Nulliparous women 
 Teens
 Immediately post partum/post abortion
 Women with a history of ectopic pregnancy
 Can’t be used by:
 Pregnant women
 Women who want pregnancy in 1-2 years
 Active STI or cervicitis
 Chronic pelvic pain
Extremely 
Effective
IUD Myths

Comparing IUDs
Copper (Paraguard)
 10-12 years
 Failure rate is 0.8%
 Changes pH of uterine lining
 Wants regular menses
 Needs to avoid hormones
 No hx of dysmenorrhea or 
menorrhagia
Levonorgestrel (progestin) 3-8 
years depends on brank
(Mirena [8], Kyleena [5], Liletta [7], 
Sklya [3])
Thicken cervical mucus, thin uterine 
lining & prevents sperm from reaching 
egg & prevents implantation
 5- years
 Failure rate 0.2%
 Amenorrhea is acceptable
 Irregular bleeding is acceptable
 History of menorrhagia or 
dysmenorrhea

Hormonal Methods
 Implants- single rod implanted under skin releases small amounts 
of progestin- lasts 3yrs failure rate 0.05%
 Oral Contraceptives- Must be taken as directed
 Most are 28 day packs with 7 days of placebo.
 Early OCs had 150 mcg estrogen 9 mg progesterone
 Today: 20mcg estrogen/progestin
 Combined both estrogen and progestin: Tri-phasic (changing 
levels of hormones) or Monophasic (steady state) 
 Prevent pregnancy by suppressing ovulation by adding 
estrogen and progesterone mimicking pregnancy.
 GnRH (gonadotropin releasing hormone) is suppress
 This then suppresses FSH and LH

Hormonal Methods Cont.
 Mini-pill or Progestin only pill- failure rate 9%
 Good choice for women who can’t take estrogen
 Breast-feeding mothers
 Women who have history of breast or gyn cancer
 Extended Pills- No placebos.  Taken continuously for 3 months at 
a time: 4 “periods” a year
 Hormonal Patch or Vaginal Ring- failure rate 9%
 Same pregnancy prevention as orals-different delivery system
 Worn for 3 weeks at a time then 1 week off
 Patch not good for women over 198 lbs
 Depo-provera: Injectable progestin-every 3 months
 Failure rate 6%

Patient Education for 
Hormonal Methods
 Begin as soon as possible
 Use a back-up method for 7 days
 Condoms should be used to prevent STIs
 Smoking while on hormonal methods increases risk for 
blood clots

Missed or Late Hormonal 
Contraception
Combined Oral 
Contraceptive 
Pills
• Take missed pill as soon as remembered and next pill at 
regular time
• Use back-up method for one week if missed1-2 pills at the 
start of pack or 3 or more pills in the first 3 weeks of pack 
Progestin Only 
Pills
• Take missed pill as soon as remembered and next pill at 
regular time
• Use back-up method for two days if pill is taken more than 3 
hours past regular time
Very 
Effective
Transdermal 
Patch
• Use back-up method for one week if patch has been on more 
than 9 days, off more than 7 days or falls off and is not 
reaffixed within 24 hours
Vaginal Ring
• Use back-up method for one week if ring has been in more 
than 5 weeks, out more than 7 days or falls out and is not 
reinserted within 3 hours

Very 
Effective
Contraindications: Combined 
Hormonal Contraception
• Clotting disorders
• History of deep vein thrombosis or 
pulmonary embolism
• Migraine with aura or focal neurological 
deficit
• Uncontrolled hypertension
• Smokers over age of 35

Side Effects: 
Hormonal Contraception
Very 
Effective
Estrogen-Related
• Breast tenderness
• Nausea
• Vomiting 
• Headaches
• Elevated blood pressure 
(rare)
Progestin-Related
• Bloating
• Anxiety
• Irritability
• Depression
• Menstrual irregularities
• Reduced libido

Menstrual-related health benefits:
•Decreased dysmenorrhea
•Decreased menstrual blood loss and anemia
•May reduce PMS symptoms
Decreased risk of:
• Ectopic pregnancies
• Endometrial and ovarian cancer 
• Benign breast conditions
• PID
Very 
Effective
Health Benefits: Combined 
Hormonal Contraception

Pros and Cons of Periods
 100 years ago average age of menarche was 16
 Higher number of pregnancies, breast-feeding and earlier 
menopause: Women had an average of 45 menstrual 
cycles during their life span.  
 Today women can have 450 menstrual cycles
 Increased estrogen exposure
 Decreased benefits of breast-feeding 
 Increased risk for Anemia

Moderately Effective
 Barrier methods
 Diaphragm 2 yrs lifespan remove within 24 hrs
 Cervical Cap 1 yr lifespan remove within 48 hours
 Both: Apply spermicide to cover inside of device
 Leave in place for at least 6 hours
 Insert additional spermicide into vagina with each sexual 
intercourse act.
 Wash with mild soap, air dry and store in carrying container.  
 May need to be refitted with significant weight gain or loss
 Vaginal Sponge-Single use: spermicide embedded in 
sponge: same concept as diaphragm or cervical cap.
Barrier Methods

Natural Family Planning: Fertility 
Awareness
• “Rhythm method”: Tracking menstrual cycle for 6 cycles to determine fertile 
period. Day 1 is 1st day of menstruation
• Subtract 18 days from longest = 1st fertile day
• Subtract 11 days from shortest= last fertile day
• Mark on calendar
• Multiple Apps for tracking, some examples: Flo, Glow, Fertility Friend 
 Fertility Awareness Method Birth-control FAMB
 Basal body temp: BEFORE getting out of bed EVERY DAY
 96-98 o  not ovulating. 97-99 o ovulating
 Cervical Mucus
 Chart mucus daily: slippery most fertile
 Sympto-thermal 
 combo of Temp and Mucus
Effective

Inform Your Patients about 
Emergency Contraception
 Prevents pregnancy after sex-
 One Step-up to 72 hours after unprotected sex
 Next-Step-2 pills 120 hours
 Not an abortifacent 
 Not the same as abortion pill 
(RU-486/mifepristone)
 Copper IUD insertion- up to 5 days post intercourse

Emergency Contraception:
Plan B® One-Step and Generic Two Pills
• Most effective when taken sooner
• One-Step can be taken up to 3 days after 
unprotected intercourse/contraceptive failure 
(up to 5 days for generic two pills)
• Taking generic 2 pills at once increases 
compliance without more side effects

Emergency 
Contraception
 Common hormonal preparations
 This probably inhibits ovulation, impairs embryo 
transport & blocks implantation-won’t interrupt an 
already established pregnancy 
 Plan B-OTC, take asap or with in 72 hours of 
unprotected intercourse, efficacy greater the 
sooner it is taken-reduces risk of pregnancy from 
8% to 1%
 Yuzpe method-4 combined OC pills, take 2 asap 
& 2 12 hours later, should be started asap or 
within 120 hours of unprotected intercourse-
slightly less effective than Plan B

Fertility Awareness
 This method is natural family planning
 Avoiding intercourse at fertile periods
 Best estimate of fertility is 5 days before ovulation & the day of 
ovulation, +/- 2 days
 Can use ovulation calendar or BBT (temp must be taken before 
getting up, temp rises .4 F with ovulation)
 Abstinence or barrier methods should be used during this time, 
not as effective for nursing mothers, women with irregular 
menses or women who stopped hormonal contraception within 
3 months

Spinnbarkeit
Natural Family Planning

Withdrawal & Abstinence
 Withdrawal-removal of penis before 
ejaculation, ineffective 2nd to 
preejaculatory droplets
 Highly dependent on user motivation
 Abstinence-effective in pregnancy & 
STD prevention, difficult at times to 
overcomes natural biological desires

Female Sterilization
 All procedures are considered to be permanent 
 Counseling must be thorough and consent must be 
signed 30 days prior to procedure
 Patient may change their mind right up to time of 
procedure
 Many different ways of doing tubaligation-rings, electro 
coagulation or clips can be used
 HSG (Hysterosalpingography) is done 3 months after procedure 
to ensure success, contraception must be used until 
then
Female Sterilization
Vasectomy
Method Failure

Elective Abortion
 AKA termination of pregnancy
 Procedure is a D&C (curettage) until 12 weeks EGA, then it is a 
D&E (evacuation)
 Legal in some states until 23 weeks EGA
 Many reasons for TOP
 All options must be offered
 Encourage involvement of significant others
 Emotional support is very important

Abortion Bans 
:
 12 STATES ban abortion as 
early as 6 weeks, before many 
people know they are pregnant: 
GA, ID, IA, KY, LA, MS, ND, OH,
 OK, SC, TN, TX.
Abortion Bans from 8-14 Weeks:
 3 STATES ban abortion between 
8-14 weeks: AR, MO, TN.
 Bans after 8 weeks: MO, TN.
 Bans after 10 weeks: TN.
 Bans after 12 weeks: AR, TN.
 Bans after 14 weeks: MO.
Abortion Bans from 15-18 Weeks:
 6 STATES ban abortion between 
15-18 weeks: AR, LA, MO, MS, 
TN, UT.
 Bans after 15 weeks: LA, MS, TN.
 Bans after 18 weeks: AR, MO, TN, 
UT.
Abortion Bans from 20-22 Weeks:
 24 STATES ban abortion after 20-
22 weeks: AL, AR, AZ, GA, ID, IN, 
IA, KS, KY, LA, MS, MO, MT, NE, 
NC, ND, OH, OK, SC,
 SD, TN, TX, WV, WI.
 6 STATES ban abortion at 20 
weeks: AZ, MS, MO, MT, NC, TN.
 19 STATES ban abortion at 22 
weeks: AL, AR, GA, ID, IN, IA, KS, 
KY, LA, NE, ND, OH, OK, SC, SD, 
TN, TX, WV, WI.

Elective Termination/Abortion
 In 2025 there were 1,126,000 terminations in the US (Guttmacher 
Institute)
 93.5% were @ < 13weeks
 63% were early medical abortions 
< 10 weeks gestation
Dosing: 
Day 1Mifepristone 200 milligrams (mg) as a single dose 
2 days later by 800 micrograms (mcg) (four-200 mcg tablets) of misoprostol 
as a single dose sub-lingual 
 Contraindications-ectopic preg, IUD insitu, Chronic renal failure, long term 
systemic corticosteroid therapy, allergy to meds, hemorrhagic disorders, 
anticoagulant therapy
 2 visits-initial & 1-2 wk follow up
